description: A Website that tells the story of abandoned equipments, which currently so called lost but we bring it back to life with our most heart touching story through stunning website.
summary:
STILL — Abandoned, Not Forgotten is an interactive archival storytelling experience that chronicles thirteen silent NASA spacecraft resting across the Moon, Mars, and deep space—from the Apollo Lunar Modules, ALSEP retroreflectors, and Surveyor 3 on the Moon to Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Viking, InSight, and Ingenuity on Mars, and outward to Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker, Kepler, and Pioneer 10.

Addressing the "Abandoned, But Not Forgotten" challenge, STILL pairs first-person spacecraft perspectives and long-form historical narrative with verified NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) records, orbital coordinates, and real-time light-delay telemetry. Readers can fire a simulated 2.56-second laser pulse to lunar retroreflectors, compare "Then & Now" orbital imagery, and explore mission longevity counters across dual Vacuum and Archival Paper reading modes.

These machines are not space debris; they are humanity’s first off-world archaeological monuments—transforming cold telemetry into an enduring human story of exploration.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

STILL — Abandoned, Not Forgotten is an interactive digital exhibition and archival storytelling platform dedicated to thirteen pioneering NASA spacecraft left behind across the Solar System:

  • Act I · The Moon: Apollo Lunar Module Descent Stages (1969-059C), Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicles (1971-063C), ALSEP & Laser Retroreflectors (1969-099C), and Surveyor 3 (1967-035A).
  • Act II · Mars: Sojourner (1996-068A), Spirit & Opportunity (2003-027A / 2003-032A), Viking 1 & 2 Landers (1975-075C), Phoenix & InSight (2018-042A), and the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (2020-052B).
  • Act III · Deep Space: Dawn at Ceres (2007-043A), NEAR Shoemaker on Asteroid 433 Eros (1996-008A), the Kepler Space Telescope (2009-011A), and Pioneer 10 (1972-012A).

As readers travel outward from Earth (384,400 km to 24+ billion km), the platform dynamically updates real-time distance and speed-of-light signal delay telemetry (1.28 seconds at the Moon to over 22 hours in interstellar space) and calculates live "Silent for N Days" counters from each mission’s final contact date.

Each chapter weaves together:

  1. First-Person Spacecraft Voice: An evocative opening transmission spoken from the resting hardware’s perspective, paired with a strict historical verification note.
    • Ping the Moon (ALSEP): Fires a simulated laser pulse across 384,400 km to the Apollo corner-cube prisms and times the exact 2.56-second round-trip photon return.
    • Sol Odometer (Spirit & Opportunity): Visualizes Opportunity’s 90-sol warranty stretching into 5,111 sols of exploration.
    • Flight Counter (Ingenuity): Maps all 72 Martian flights against the original 5-flight technology demonstration goal.
    • Send a Message (Pioneer 10): Broadcasts a radio signal into interstellar space at 299,792 km/s to illustrate the immense scale of deep space.
    • Then & Now Archival Sliders: Compares surface photography from active operations with modern orbital reconnaissance imagery from LRO and HiRISE.
  2. Verified NSSDCA Colophon & Master Registry: Links every mission directly to its official NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) catalog entry.

Creative Design & Dual Reading Modes

Rather than building a conventional dashboard, we designed STILL as a tactile museum monograph with two distinct physical reading environments:

  • Vacuum Mode (Dark): An obsidian zero-gravity canvas (#07080a) featuring a custom HTML5 Canvas 3D starfield with inertial scroll physics and a two-stage radial time-warp interaction when clicking the STILL masthead.
  • Paper Mode (Light): A vintage 1969 cotton-rag archival parchment sheet (#e6dac2) with fine paper grain, Celestial Cartography graticule lines, and high-friction page-turn mechanics.
  • Editorial Rubrication: Key historical dates, chapter numbers, and opening initials are highlighted in archival Rubric Red (--c-rubric) set in calibrated Space Mono typography so critical milestones anchor the reader’s eye effortlessly.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Humanizing Space Hardware: Shifts public perception of decommissioned spacecraft from "discarded equipment" to irreplaceable off-world archaeological monuments and active scientific benchmarks.
  • Accessible Science Communication: Translates abstract astrophysical numbers (light-time delay, sols, heliocentric distances, NSSDCA designators) into intuitive, hands-on interactions for students, educators, and space enthusiasts.
  • Strict Historical Integrity: Separates poetic storytelling from hard telemetry through automated build-time schema validation against NASA/NSSDCA records.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Framework & Content Architecture: Astro 5 (astro:content MDX collections), TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3 Custom Properties.
  • Data Validation: Zod strict schema validation (STRICT_FACTS=true) verifying NSSDCA IDs, coordinates, distances, and mission dates at build time.
  • Motion & Graphics: Custom HTML5 2D Canvas starfield and celestial graticule engine, GSAP + ScrollTrigger, Lenis mode-aware smooth scrolling, and custom SVG schematics.
  • Data & Imagery Sources: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC), Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (HiRISE), and NASA/JPL-Caltech archives.

Key Factors Considered by Our Team

  1. Scientific Accuracy vs. Emotional Resonance: We separated verified NSSDCA facts (data/artifacts.ts) from narrative prose (story/chapters/*.mdx) so poetic storytelling never compromises factual accuracy.
  2. Reading Ergonomics & Universal Responsiveness: We calibrated Space Mono line lengths (70ch), line height (1.92), and word spacing across all screen dimensions (320px mobile viewports to 4K displays).
  3. Accessibility & Performance: Full prefers-reduced-motion support, keyboard navigation (← / →), semantic ARIA live telemetry regions, and zero-overhead static site generation.
